intro: Architects can earn more money by shifting from manual, retrospective tracking to real-time project management that monitors scope creep and fee consumption. This approach stops the bleed of uncompensated hours and allows you to catch budget overruns before they impact your bottom line.

blocks.text: The hidden cost of manual project tracking

When you rely on manual spreadsheets to track time, you are always looking backward. By the time you realize a project has exceeded its budget, those hours are already spent and unrecoverable. This disconnect is the main reason why firms struggle to maintain healthy profit margins.

The primary cause is the lack of real-time visibility. If you do not track your fee consumption against the current project phase, you are flying blind. Scope creep often happens in small increments. Without a system to flag these additions, you end up doing extra work for free.

items: Manual data entry leads to human error and delayed reporting.
Disconnected systems prevent a single source of truth for project data.
Inconsistent phase-based planning makes it hard to identify where budget leaks occur.
Lack of standardized procedures for client communication causes scope creep.

blocks.text: How to fix profitability without spending money

You can start improving your margins today by changing your internal processes. Standardize your project checklists for every phase. This ensures that every team member knows exactly what is included in the fee and what constitutes additional work.

items: Implement a strict policy of documenting every change request in writing before starting work.
Review your project hours weekly instead of monthly to identify trends early.
Use keyboard shortcuts in Excel like ⌘ + ⌥ + V to paste values only, keeping your data clean.
Set up standard email templates in Gmail to reduce time spent on repetitive client communication.
Audit your current phase-based planning to ensure it matches the actual work required.

blocks.text: If your firm has specific rules about handling client data or using third-party tools, always follow your employer's guidelines strictly.

faq.question: How can architects earn more money without taking more projects?
faq.answer: You can earn more by increasing the profitability of existing projects. Focus on tracking scope creep, reducing non-billable administrative time, and ensuring every hour worked is accounted for in your fee structure.

faq.question: What is the biggest cause of budget overruns?
faq.answer: Scope creep is the most common cause. When changes are requested but not tracked or billed, the budget is consumed by uncompensated work.

faq.question: Can I use Lazur to track my billable hours?
faq.answer: Lazur can guide you through the process of entering time into your preferred tracker or help you draft notes about your daily tasks, but it does not automatically click buttons or log hours for you.
